one_liner: Small Rust TrueType glyph rasterizer (dense accumulation buffer plus prefix sum); 2016 author numbers claim 4-7.6x over FreeType 2.6.5.
what_it_does: font-rs parses a TrueType (glyf/loca) font from a borrowed byte slice (font::parse) and renders one glyph id at an integer pixels-per-em size into an 8-bit grayscale coverage bitmap (Font::render_glyph(glyph_id, size) returns a GlyphBitmap with width, height, left, top and data). It also offers cmap format 4 code point lookup and hhea/hmtx metrics. It is not a FreeType drop-in: there is no face/size/slot API, no hinting, no CFF outlines, no subpixel positioning, and the README calls the code rough and 'basically not ready for prime time'.
how_it_is_fast: It is an accumulation-buffer (signed-area) scanline rasterizer in the libart/FreeType-smooth family, but instead of sorting cells into a sparse structure it writes exact-area coverage deltas for every line segment straight into a dense f32 array (Raster::draw_line, about 100 lines in src/raster.rs), which avoids branch mispredictions. Quadratic Beziers are flattened into n evenly spaced line segments with n derived from the curve's deviation (not recursive subdivision). One prefix-sum pass then turns the deltas into 8-bit coverage; the optional 'sse' feature does that four floats at a time with shift-and-add, min, truncating convert and a byte shuffle. Glyph parsing is pull-style iterators over the raw glyf data, so no point or curve arrays are allocated.
when_to_use: Learning, porting or vendoring the original dense accumulation rasterizer: src/raster.rs plus src/accumulate.rs are about 230 lines of Apache-2.0 Rust excluding tests, and fontdue, ab_glyph_rasterizer and golang.org/x/image/vector follow the same design.
Rasterizing grayscale coverage masks for a glyph atlas from trusted TrueType (glyf) fonts at integer pixel sizes, in Rust, with zero crate dependencies.
Larger glyph sizes, where the author's snippet-only 2016 numbers show the widest gap to FreeType (about 7.6x with the SIMD accumulate).

As a reference implementation when writing a C++ rasterizer: the algorithm is short enough to port directly, and FreeType's own GSoC 2022 'dense' module (branch gsoc-anurag-2022-final, src/dense) is a C port of it.
when_not_to_use: Untrusted or user-supplied fonts: parse() unwraps missing head/maxp tables and slices table offsets without range checks, so malformed files panic (issues #12 'Out-of-bounds path nodes shouldn't panic' and #44 'Potential wrapping add' are still open).
CFF/CFF2 OpenType, variable fonts, colour or bitmap glyphs, or code points above U+FFFF (only cmap format 4 is read; lookup_glyph_id returns None above 0xFFFF).
Small UI text that needs hinting or LCD subpixel rendering, or text that needs fractional sizes or subpixel x positions (size is a u32 and the glyph origin is snapped to whole pixels).

Projects that need a maintained dependency: last commit 2020-09-05, 9 open issues, 3 open PRs, and the crates.io release (0.1.3, 2018-07-09, 8,212 downloads, one reverse dependency) predates the Rust SIMD port, the metrics API and the out-of-bounds fixes on master.
Expecting the 2016 gap against current FreeType: FreeType's smooth rasterizer was sped up afterwards (2.11, 2021, per search snippets), and no current head-to-head numbers are public.

integration.dependencies: none (Cargo.toml lists no dependencies; the 'sse' feature uses std::arch on master, while the crates.io 0.1.3 release still builds the C SSE module through build.rs)
integration.min_toolchain: Stable Rust for the library (CI built and tested on stable, beta and nightly; Cargo.toml has no edition, so edition 2015); nightly Rust for the benches (#![feature(test)]). No rust-version is declared.
integration.platforms: any for the scalar build; the 'sse' feature is x86/x86-64 only, chosen at compile time with no runtime CPU detection (issue #29 open), and uses _mm_shuffle_epi8, an SSSE3 instruction despite the feature name
integration.thread_safety: not documented; from the source, Font borrows the font bytes immutably and render_glyph(&self) allocates a fresh Raster per call, with no shared mutable state

gotchas: The 'sse' accumulate does unaligned 4-float loads up to 3 floats past the end of its input slice; it stays inside the allocation only because Raster::new pads its buffer by 4 floats. accumulate() is public, and its own unit tests call it on unpadded Vecs of length 1-7, so those tests read past the allocation (undefined behaviour in Rust; not behind the published numbers).
The library prints to stdout: render_glyph prints 'glyph N error' and returns None for empty glyphs such as the space, and 'unhandled glyph case' for empty compound components.

Compound glyphs are rendered recursively with no depth limit, and only the ARGS_ARE_XY_VALUES component form is handled (a TODO in src/font.rs); a font with cyclic components would recurse until the stack overflows.

Coverage is scaled by 255 and truncated (issue #13 suggests 256-epsilon), and the SIMD and scalar prefix sums add in a different order, so 'sse' and non-'sse' builds are not guaranteed bit-identical; the unit tests only check hand-picked inputs.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick font-rs only to study or vendor the original ~230-line rasterizer core; for an application, fontdue (same accumulation design, maintained, TrueType and OpenType, its own latency plots against FreeType) is the better choice, and ttf-parser is the better choice if you only need outlines to feed your own rasterizer.
verified_claims_summary: Snippet only: the author's 2016 post timed rendering the glyph 'g' from Roboto Regular at 1-200 px/em on a 2.9 GHz Xeon E5-2690 against FreeType 2.6.5 and reports about 7.6x faster at larger sizes with the SIMD accumulate, over 4x at 12 px/em and over 6x at 12 px/em on a CJK face. FreeType's load flags and hinting mode, the compilers and the harness could not be checked (the post and the freetype-devel threads are blocked), and the repo's benches time font-rs alone; the measured code was the 2016 C SSE3 accumulate, which master replaced with a Rust std::arch port in 2018.
status_note: Abandoned (last commit 2020-09-05, crates.io release from 2018) and self-described as not production-ready, but Apache-2.0, dependency-free and small enough to vendor or port.
